title: Zeroth Fitting ideal on an algebraic space and its pullback
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use modules on the small etale structure sheaves, quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback and module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it admits an exact presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite, and of finite type if etale locally finitely generated. For every finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $M$ on an algebraic space $X$, there is a unique quasi-coherent ideal $\operatorname{Fit}_0(M)\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ whose restriction to every affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ is the ideal sheaf associated to the zeroth Fitting ideal of the $A$-module $M(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ [def-trf-fitting-ideal-zero]. This is the ideal generated by all maximal kernel-row determinants of any finite free generating surjection, including the unit ideal when the target module is zero and the free source has rank zero. The ideal $\operatorname{Fit}_0(M)$ is of finite type. For every morphism $g:X\prime\to X$ of algebraic spaces, $g^*M$ is finitely presented quasi-coherent and $$\operatorname{Fit}_0(g^*M)=\operatorname{im}(g^*\operatorname{Fit}_0(M)\to\mathcal O_{X\prime}).$$ The equality is one of ideal subsheaves and does not assert injectivity of $g^*\operatorname{Fit}_0(M)\to\mathcal O_{X\prime}$.

proof.text: For each etale scheme chart $u:U\to X$, the cartesian-chart-family equivalence restricts $M$ to a quasi-coherent module $M_U$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. Use the Zariski--etale quasi-coherent equivalence to regard this as an ordinary quasi-coherent module $\overline M_U$ on $U$. It is finite type: on every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$, the affine-chart calculus makes its sections a finitely presented, hence finitely generated, $A$-module. Form the ordinary scheme ideal $J_U=\operatorname{Fit}_0(\overline M_U)$ using the scheme Fitting-ideal theorem, and transfer its inclusion into $\mathcal O_U$ back to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. For a chart map $a:V\to U$ over $X$, that theorem gives $J_V=\operatorname{im}(a^*J_U\to\mathcal O_V)$. Here $a$ is etale, so tensor pullback is restriction, preserving the inclusion into the restricted structure sheaf by the etale specialization of the chart-tensor theorem. Thus this image equality identifies $a^*J_U$ with $J_V$ as submodules of $\mathcal O_V$. The scheme/etale comparison commutes with these pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 0CZ3 (section-fitting-ideals), construction from scheme Fitting ideals and the cartesian chart description Tag 03LZ.

proof.text: The identifications of the ideals $J_U$ in step 1 satisfy the identity and composition conditions: both competing maps have the same composite with the inclusion into the structure sheaf, and that inclusion is a monomorphism. Their inclusions form a compatible family of maps to $\mathcal O_U$. The cartesian-chart-family equivalence therefore gives a quasi-coherent module $J$ and a map $J\to\mathcal O_X$. Its kernel is quasi-coherent by the kernels/colimits theorem and restricts to zero on all affine etale charts by the kernel clause of the affine-chart calculus; hence it is zero, so this map is an ideal inclusion. On $\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, the affine clause of the scheme Fitting-ideal theorem identifies $J$ with the associated sheaf of $\operatorname{Fit}_0(M(\operatorname{Spec}A))$. The ring independence theorem identifies that ideal with the maximal kernel-row determinants of every finite free surjection. A second ideal having these affine restrictions has the same inclusions on all affine opens of every chart. The identities there glue, and the fully faithful cartesian-chart equivalence gives a unique isomorphism commuting with inclusion into $\mathcal O_X$. Thus the ideal subsheaves are equal. Set $\operatorname{Fit}_0(M)=J$.

source.place: Tag 0CZ3 (section-fitting-ideals), characterization on every affine etale chart; Tag 03LZ (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent-small-etale).

proof.text:
Fix an affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$. Its section module $N$ is finitely presented by the affine-chart calculus, so choose $A^m\to A^n\to N\to0$ as in the definition of finite presentation. Write $r_1,\ldots,r_m\in A^n$ for the images of the standard basis, generating the kernel. If $z_i=\sum_{j=1}^m a_{ij}r_j$ for $1\le i\le n$, expanding the determinant by its defining Leibniz formula gives
$$\det(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=\sum_{(j_1,\ldots,j_n)\in\{1,\ldots,m\}^n}\left(\prod_{i=1}^n a_{ij_i}\right)\det(r_{j_1},\ldots,r_{j_n}).$$
Every determinant on the right is itself a kernel-row determinant. Hence the kernel-row ideal is generated by this finite list of at most $m^n$ elements. For $n=0$, the list is the single empty determinant $1$; for $m=0<n$, all kernel rows are zero and the ideal is zero. The finite-type clause of the affine-chart calculus now proves that $J$ is of finite type. This is the finite determinant expansion in Tag 07ZA(4), rather than an additional Fitting-ideal lemma.

Let $g:X'\to X$ be arbitrary. Choose a surjective etale family of affine schemes $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to X$. The fibre-product/covering theorem gives an etale covering $X'\times_XU_i\to X'$. Cover each of these spaces by affine etale charts $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Write $v:V\to X'$ and $a:V\to U_i$; thus $gv=u_i a$. Tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence. The composition and etale-restriction clauses of the chart-tensor theorem identify $(g^*M)|_V$ with $a^*(M|_{U_i})$. After the Zariski--etale comparison, the affine pullback-sections theorem identifies its sections with $B\otimes_{A_i}N_i$, where $N_i=M(U_i)$. The same comparison applies to $J$ and to its inclusion, since the affine theorem is natural in module maps. In particular $(g^*J)|_V$ corresponds to $B\otimes_{A_i}J(U_i)$, and its canonical map to $\mathcal O_V$ sends $b\otimes j$ to $b\rho(j)$, where $\rho:A_i\to B$ is induced by $a$. This formula is the local tensor formula of the chart-tensor theorem; all identifications preserve the specified adjunction units.

source.place: Tag 0CZ4 (lemma-base-change-fitting-ideal), etale localization; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03FX, 03GA, 03LV; descent.tex Tag 03LC; schemes.tex Tag 01I9.

proof.text: Each $N_i$ in step 4 is finitely presented by the affine-chart calculus. The module base-change lemma implies that $B\otimes_{A_i}N_i$ is finitely presented over $B$, for every ring map $A_i\to B$. Its finite presentation gives an exact finite free presentation of the associated module on $V$ by the affine-chart calculus. The charts $V$ cover $X'$ by step 4, so these presentations give precisely the etale-local finite presentations required in the statement. Together with quasi-coherence from step 4 this proves that $g^*M$ is finitely presented quasi-coherent; thus steps 1--2 also construct $\operatorname{Fit}_0(g^*M)$.

source.place: Tag 0CZ4 (lemma-base-change-fitting-ideal), pullback module; spaces-properties.tex section-properties-modules, preservation of finite presentation under pullback.

proof.text:
On each chart $V$ of step 4, put $I_i=J(U_i)=\operatorname{Fit}_0(N_i)$. The image of $B\otimes_{A_i}I_i\to B$, $b\otimes j\mapsto b\rho(j)$, consists exactly of finite sums of these products, namely $\rho(I_i)B$. Pullbacks of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent, their images are quasi-coherent by the kernels/colimits theorem, and the affine-chart calculus computes those image sheaves by the images of these module maps. The ring Fitting base-change theorem gives
$$\operatorname{Fit}_0(B\otimes_{A_i}N_i)=\rho(\operatorname{Fit}_0(N_i))B=\rho(I_i)B.$$
The affine characterization in steps 1--2 therefore makes the restrictions of $\operatorname{Fit}_0(g^*M)$ and $\operatorname{im}(g^*J\to\mathcal O_{X'})$ the same submodule of $\mathcal O_V$. Since these charts cover $X'$, membership of a section in either ideal can be checked locally and the sheaf condition glues the identical local sections. Hence the ideal subsheaves are equal globally. Only the image of the tensor map was used; its injectivity is unnecessary.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_zerothFittingIdeal {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (M : X.Modules) (hM : M.IsFinitePresentation) (hqc : M.IsQuasicoherent) : ∃ I : QuasiCoherentIdeal X, IsZerothFittingIdeal M I ∧ (∀ J : QuasiCoherentIdeal X, IsZerothFittingIdeal M J → J = I) ∧ (I.val : X.Modules).IsFiniteType ∧ ∀ (X' : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : X' ⟶ X), ((moduleTensorPullback g).obj M).IsFinitePresentation ∧ ((moduleTensorPullback g).obj M).IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∃ I' : QuasiCoherentIdeal X', IsZerothFittingIdeal ((moduleTensorPullback g).obj M) I' ∧ I'.val = Subobject.mk (image.ι (idealTensorMap g I))
